newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The labour component of the National Empowerment Consortium (NEC) will form a new investment vehicle to finance the unions' 17.5 percent stake in Johnnies Industrial Corp, raising capital from union-linked institutions by offering Johnnic shares at a discount.

- The Congress of South African Trade Unions' investment trust has put together a consortium with other black groups to submit a bid for a controlling stake in Protea Assurance, owned by UK group Royal Sun Alliance.
- Eskom is planning to spend five billion rand over the next five years on upgrading and expanding the electricity transmission network in South Africa and Africa.
- A senior fund manager has claimed that he was sacked by UK investment bank Kleinwort Benson because he questioned South African ministers in a critical manner.

- The investigation by the Office for Serious Economic Offences into pyramid scheme Sun Multi Serve's operations had uncovered theft amounting to "millions of rands", a spokesman for the office said on Friday.

- The ANC seemed still to regard boycotts as legitimate, since it had taken no action against Deputy Environment Minister Peter Mokaba for not paying the rates on his Sandton house, DP Johannesburg councillor Mike Moriarty said yesterday.
- South African rugby faces another crisis with the imminent resignation of Ray Mordt as national selector.

- The South African government launched $300 million of dollar-denominated bonds, or Yankee bonds, in the U.S. market on Friday, $50 million more than was originally planned, Merrill Lynch, the lead manager, said on Friday.
- South African Druggists has acquired 100 percent control of Medicross, South Africa's largest private clinic operator.
- Tony Blair, the leader of the British Labour Party, has pledged to support South Africa in its increasingly fierce dispute with the European Union on a free trade agreement.

- In what is seen as a bid to provide some security to holders of low-voting "N" shares, the controlling shareholders involved in the 5.3 billion rand merger between Adcock Ingram and Premier Pharmaceutical have agreed not to accept any future offer for control from a third party "unless an identical offer is extended to the holders of the N shares".
- Widespread anger and calls for the dismissal of Springbok team boss Andre Markgraaff have greeted the sacking of Francois Pienaar as South Africa's rugby captain.

- General Magnus Malan, acquitted of all charges against him in the KwaMakhutha murder trial, said at the weekend he was going to play a more active role protecting the soldiers who fought under his command.
